scams.name: Tainan Airbnb & Minsu Off-Platform Deposit Fraud
scams.tldr: Tainan's charm as Taiwan's cultural capital draws tourists to its Historic District and Anping Old Street, where a dense network of minsu (family-run guesthouses) and Airbnb properties creates an off-platform payment risk.
scams.description: Tainan's charm as Taiwan's cultural capital draws tourists to its Historic District and Anping Old Street, where a dense network of minsu (family-run guesthouses) and Airbnb properties creates an off-platform payment risk. A 2025 traveler report titled 'Is this a scam or is this typical for booking accommodations?' captured the pattern — a Tainan-area minsu requested payment in cash on arrival plus a credit-card hold for deposit, after the Booking.com reservation showed no payment required.
scams.avoidance: Book Tainan accommodations only through Airbnb, Booking.com, Agoda, or a verified minsu website with a Tourism Administration license. Never pay a Tainan minsu deposit via LINE Pay, Western Union, wire transfer, or gift cards under any circumstances. Pay bank transfers only to a Taiwan Post Office or named local bank (Cathay, CTBC, Mega, First) — never overseas accounts. Cross-check listing photos and the address on Google Maps Street View before paying any deposit. Dispute fraudulent bookings with your card issuer within 30 days and file a Tainan Police report at +886 6 229 5366.
scams.location: Tainan Historic District short-term rentals, Anping Old Street guesthouses, Shennong Street minsu properties, Ten Drums Cultural Village area lodging, Tainan National Cheng Kung University perimeter rentals

scams.name: Anping Old Street & Tainan Market Souvenir Receipt Padding
scams.tldr: Tainan's Anping Old Street is Taiwan's oldest tourist shopping strip, dating to Dutch-colonial occupation in the 1600s, and its foot traffic creates the same receipt-padding conditions that Taiwan News documented at Ximending on 4 March 2026 — a South Korean tourist was charged NT$500 extra for a tea item she never purchased at a Taipei souvenir shop.
scams.description: Tainan's Anping Old Street is Taiwan's oldest tourist shopping strip, dating to Dutch-colonial occupation in the 1600s, and its foot traffic creates the same receipt-padding conditions that Taiwan News documented at Ximending on 4 March 2026 — a South Korean tourist was charged NT$500 extra for a tea item she never purchased at a Taipei souvenir shop. The Anping variant targets Tainan day-trippers with similar mechanics.
scams.avoidance: Ask the price of every item before it is rung up at any Anping, Shennong Street, or Tainan market stall. Demand an itemized receipt and cross-check line items against the bag before leaving the counter. Buy tea and dried goods at registered Tainan tea shops, not night-market street stalls, for fair posted prices. Pay by credit card for purchases over NT$500 so a chargeback is possible if the charge does not match goods received. Call Taiwan's consumer-protection hotline 1950 from inside the shop if overcharged for immediate resolution.
scams.location: Anping Old Street souvenir stalls, Tainan Flower Night Market food and snack rows, Shennong Street tourist-facing vendors, Dadong Night Market Anping perimeter, Hayashi Department Store old quarter, Confucius Temple Culture Park vendors

scams.name: Tainan AI Fake-Police & Spoofed-Number Phone Scam
scams.tldr: A Taiwan-wide 2025-2026 scam surge reached Tainan via the same AI video-impersonation pattern that the Taichung District Prosecutors Office indicted 18 operators for on 22 April 2026, per Taipei Times reporting.
scams.description: A Taiwan-wide 2025-2026 scam surge reached Tainan via the same AI video-impersonation pattern that the Taichung District Prosecutors Office indicted 18 operators for on 22 April 2026, per Taipei Times reporting. The scam uses spoofed caller-ID to impersonate Taiwanese or Chinese law enforcement, followed by a live video call with a man in uniform claiming to be a police officer or prosecutor.
scams.avoidance: Hang up immediately on any inbound call claiming to be Taiwanese or Chinese police, prosecutor, or customs official. Taiwan police do not investigate by phone or video — any call demanding payment is always a scam. Delete without clicking any SMS claiming to be from 7-Eleven, FamilyMart, or Taipower with a payment-site link. Never send cryptocurrency, gift cards, or bank transfers in response to a phone, video, or SMS demand. Report suspicious contacts to Taiwan's 165 anti-fraud hotline or Tainan Police at +886 6 229 5366.
scams.location: Tainan city-wide SMS and phone targets, Tainan hotel rooms and guesthouses, Anping District tourist rentals, Tainan West Central District residential, National Cheng Kung University area, Yongkang District residential targets
